answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 10 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and as a result paying the sparrow bond on all of them and exposing each to the sable slash. Because the shale audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A farm of 37 pays that 119 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
